chunks: “There is no harm in touching him after the ghusl and kissing him.” And that does not contradict what he narrated:

What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual washing, here referring to the washing of the deceased
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him; honorific for the Imam
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or harm; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to touch or kiss the deceased after the ghusl in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage states that there is no harm in touching or kissing the deceased after the ghusl. It then introduces a narrated report, indicating a juristic discussion about reconciling apparently differing hadith on funeral and post-death etiquette.
